title: ID0422462-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / R3 170001340] Power limitation on Tesla Y
description:
Reported behaviour/issue: Our managing director charged at the charging station on Sunday. A Tesla Y, preconditioned, low SoC. Although it was the only car on site, there was only 25 kW on the D300 for several minutes. The supermarket was closed, and there's a new and large transformer on site. Therefore, load management intervention should not affect. Only much later the power increase to > 70 kW. Strange: The Tesla app displayed the message "Power limited by charging station." There shouldn't be any power restrictions in the Sicharge? Charging took place at the main station, Outlet 1 (=DE*VIR*E227486).
Solution: Information provided. Backend is increasing the power very slowly, around every minute

additional_info.subject: AW: ID0422462-DC/Si-D/DE-[MP / R3 170001340] Power limitation on Tesla Y CRM:02682000084
additional_info.body:
Hi Francisco,
thank’s a lot for your fast investigation.
·
A period of 10 minutes for smartCharging from 25 kW to 151 kW is very very smart? Or should we say slow?
J
·
SmartCharging: Who is the leading part in communication? That’s the Sicharge, called ESVE in the log’s?
·
The max power in the log of 400 A x 400 V looks quit good. …170 kW is the maximum in Tesla’s data sheet.
·
I ask other driver of Tesla Model 3 and BMW iX … they can’t remember any delay, perhaps one or two minutes, but then they got full/available power.
·
I just called our external external electrician: At our branch in Füssen we have an ELM, but in fact no limitation (only protection against overload and possibility of legal shutdown by the local power network operator)
·
I read latest Siemens release notes
o
v6.0.3. … optimized Dynamic Power Allocation (DPA) … there are any parameters for fine tuning?
o
v7.0.5 …new major update. I didn’t see any key features for us. But perhaps any improvement for our Volvos or Ivecos? …next week Catalina can give us an advice for Mauerstetten and our public Sicharges
Viele Grüße
Martin Glöckner

Hi Martin,
Here is the SmartCharging profile that is sent via your backend to our charger. As you can see the setpoints are set to 13kW at the beginning and then in the backend logic it changes over time. We just receive this information from your side and translate it.
[
{
"connectorId": 1,
"csChargingProfiles": {
"chargingProfileId": 2,
"stackLevel": 0,
"chargingProfilePurpose": "TxDefaultProfile",
"chargingProfileKind": "Absolute",
"chargingSchedule": {
"startSchedule": "2025-05-06T11:08:57.000Z",
"chargingRateUnit": "W",
"chargingSchedulePeriod": [
{
"startPeriod": 0,
"limit": 13110
}
]
}
},
"status": "Accepted"
},
{
"connectorId": 2,
"csChargingProfiles": {
"chargingProfileId": 3,
"stackLevel": 0,
"chargingProfilePurpose": "TxDefaultProfile",
"chargingProfileKind": "Absolute",
"chargingSchedule": {
"startSchedule": "2025-05-06T11:28:57.000Z",
"chargingRateUnit": "W",
"chargingSchedulePeriod": [
{
"startPeriod": 0,
"limit": 13110
}
]
}
}
}
]
Below, you can see the difference in time.
Except for that singular 15sec, all the other Power setpoints were done with a 1min delay. This looks like a configuration from the backend where the backend only updates the values each minute, hence why the longer it took.
Please ask the backend provider for more detailed information. From our side, we are not allowed to change this value only read it.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
